newsitem.title: USA: U.S. stock index futures open higher.
newsitem.headline: U.S. stock index futures open higher.

text.p: U.S. stock index futures opened higher, still buoyant after huge gains during Thursday's shortened trading session.
September Standard and Poor's 500 futures soared to a new record high of 929.00 on Thursday and continued gains to reach 931.00 in overnight trade before Monday's opening.
Traders said the long U.S. Independence day holiday weekend did little to dampen an overall bullish view of U.S. stocks after Thursday's record.
"I don't think there's anything to get in our way today," an S&P 500 futures trader said.
He said he expected a "slow rally higher" during the session and pegged the most significant resistance at 935.00. Other topside levels include 933.20 and 937.50, traders said.
One floor trader warned that 927.50 was a support level to watch should gains unravel. He said below there "much-needed" profit-taking could begin.
One firm pegged September S&P 500 fair value at 7.70 points premium to cash, buy programs at 9.50 points premium to cash or wider and sell programs at 6.40 points premium or narrower.
Traders noted that Monday's economic line-up was slim. The slow data week culminates with June producer price news on Friday.
"It looks like the market is on its own today," an S&P 500 floor source said.
Trading was quiet in the first half hour and September S&Ps 500s dipped briefly into negative territory in the thin volume conditions.
But traders said strong Treasury bonds and spillover from last week's gains should underpin stock indices.

They said stocks would continue to be boosted by the Federal Reserve's decision last week to hold U.S. interest rates steady. Also last week, June's U.S. jobs report dampened expectations of a rise in U.S. interest rates in the near futures.
The report showed the U.S. jobless rate rose to 5.0 percent in June from a 24-year low of 4.8 percent in May.

At 0912 CDT/1412 GMT, Sept S&P 500s were up 3.25 points at 931.00, Nasdaq 100s up 8.75 at 1010.00, Russell 2000s were flat at 401.50, Nikkei 225 index futures down 490.0 at 19,770.0 and Midcap 400s up 0.45 point to 297.75. ((Chicago Derivatives Desk: 312-408-8750)) email:derivatives@reuters.com
